title: bug: postflight-safe.mjs kills the wrapper harness at 60 min (:51), but at f38a17d4 the full postflight.ps1 takes 3200 s (5.1) and 3400 s (pwsh 7) on an idle Ryzen 9 9950X3D desktop, and windows-latest runs this work about 1.5x slower, so CI's "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight" will end in failureClass TIMEOUT now that task-02af8654 lets the job reach it (the 30-min cap did the same on 10-31, a95f7199)
description:
Filed by hunt #25 (task-9ca91400, architect-67c762f6) on 2026-11-04. Lane: the windows-latest steps after step 15, which no completed PR #230 run had reached since 2037e856 (governor comment-f95ba6c8).

PROBLEM
- scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs runs postflight.sh or postflight.ps1 with execFile `timeout: 60 * 60 * 1000` and `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'` (:51-52).
  - A kill becomes failureClass TIMEOUT and exit 1 (:55, :8).
  - The comment at :45-48 sizes that bound on "about 20 minutes on a desktop and past 30 on windows-latest".
- The harness has grown since then. Between main (3ed7a299, the dependabot PR base) and f38a17d4:
  - postflight.ps1 went from 5013 to 6165 lines;
  - postflight-vm-route.ps1 went from 0 to 1008 lines;
  - the shared postflight-worktree.cjs gained 1340 lines;
  - postflight.sh went from 5645 to 6725 lines, and postflight-vm-route.sh from 0 to 777. 9e9e7345 (CQ-M07r) then added another 255 to postflight-vm-route.sh.
  - CQ-M07s and CQ-M07t (74fe4c99, 527735ea, open) add more VM-route scenarios to both suites.

EVIDENCE
1. Desktop run of the full harness at f38a17d4, using hunt #22's CI emulation (scripts in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9ca91400/mine/: ci-lib.ps1, leg-p5.ps1, leg-p7.ps1, postflight-tee.mjs).
   - Emulation: env stripped, CI=true, a fresh HOME, an 8.3 TEMP, and the CI chain pwsh step -> node -> engine. postflight-tee.mjs repeats postflight-safe's exact execFile but keeps the output.
   - Deviation: GITHUB_ACTIONS was removed for that sub-step only. postflight.ps1:4317 is its only reader, the scenario AE symlink check this host cannot pass.
   - The host is an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D with 32 threads, at 13% CPU load sampled mid-run. The 5.1 and pwsh 7 runs overlapped.
   - Windows PowerShell 5.1: PASS in 3200 s, 89% of the cap. Verdict {"engine":"powershell","exit":0,"lastScenario":"Z","failureClass":"NONE"}. Log: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9ca91400/logs/p5-postflight-ps1-full.log, last line "rawExit=0 failure=null secs=3200".
   - pwsh 7: PASS in 3400 s, 94% of the cap. Log: logs/p7-postflight-pwsh-full.log, "secs=3400".
2. Runner against desktop, for the same kind of work (sequential PowerShell and git process spawns):
   - Live CI run 41848822541 at 9e9e7345 on windows-latest:
     - "Test Windows PowerShell landing guard" took 47 s, against 30 s on this desktop (1.57x).
     - "Test PowerShell 7 landing guard" took 45 s, against 28 s (1.61x).
   - a95f7199 (10-31): run 41198897512's "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight" was "killed at exactly 30:01", {"engine":"powershell","exit":1,"lastScenario":"Z","failureClass":"TIMEOUT"}, while the suite took about 20 min locally (1.5x or more).
   - Linux: postflight-safe bash took 1841 s in hunt #25's WSL run. ubuntu-latest's "Test Bash wrapper postflight and parity" took 2750 s at 80078651 (run 41834653023), 2692 s at 2037e856 and 2688 s at 060d7b8c. That is about 1.46x.
   - At 1.5x, 5.1 needs about 4800 s and pwsh 7 about 5100 s, against the 3600 s cap. To pass, the runner would have to be at most 12.5% slower than this desktop for 5.1, and 6% for pwsh 7.
3. Why CI has not shown it yet:
   - Since 2037e856 the windows-latest job stopped at step 15 (task-02af8654, DONE 9463e77d). Before that it stopped at the worktree suite (task-e45da220).
   - main-based runs (the dependabot PRs at 00:23Z) show main's smaller suite on windows-latest: 1846-2092 s for 5.1 and 1689-1948 s for pwsh 7.
4. Live: run 41848822541 (9e9e7345, which includes 02af8654's fix) passed windows-latest steps 15-20.
   - Step 22, "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight", began at 15:14:00Z.
   - Predicted: it fails at about 16:18Z, after worktree-landing.ps1 and then the 60-min kill. Hunt #25 adds its outcome as a comment on this row.
5. ubuntu-latest already uses about 2690 s of the same cap (76%), before CQ-M07r's 255 new vm-route.sh lines.

FIX DIRECTION
- Raise the bound in postflight-safe.mjs so that the predicted runner time fits with headroom: at least 120 min.
  - ci.yml sets no timeout-minutes, so GitHub's 360-min job default still applies.
  - Keep SIGKILL and the TIMEOUT class.
  - Replace the :45-48 comment with the measured numbers above.
- Optional: an env override for the bound. It is not needed for the fix.
- Out of scope unless the governor asks: splitting the 5.1 and pwsh 7 postflights into separate jobs to cut wall time.
  - Two steps of about 80 min each make the Windows job about 3 h.
  - The concurrency group lets the run in progress finish, so PR #230 results would lag by that much.

FILES
- scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs
- scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs
- No open row holds either (lanes.js at 15:26Z).

NOTES FOR THE PLANNER
- epic-be924fb8 has no finalTaskId, so this newest row reads isEpicFinal:true through the max-order fallback. Keep the gate narrow: `node --test scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs`.
- Do not plan a full postflight run as the gate. It takes 55-60 min per engine on this desktop.
definitionOfDone: scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bounds the harness at no less than 120 min (7,200,000 ms), still with killSignal SIGKILL and failureClass TIMEOUT on a kill. The comment at :45-48 cites measured durations (this row's 3200 s / 3400 s desktop runs and the runner ratio) instead of "about 20 minutes on a desktop and past 30 on windows-latest".

scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs has a case that fails if the bound drops below 120 min. The test reads the bound from the module (exported, not copied). `node --test scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs` passes.

The completion summary names the first PR #230 CI run that contains the change, and reports its windows-latest "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight" and "Test PowerShell 7 wrapper postflight and parity" outcomes, or says the run is still in progress.

comments.author: governor-e6142a94
comments.content:
Evidence from real CI for the planner, from the governor. The same 60-min cap is close on Linux too, so size the fix for both platforms.
- On PR #230's ubuntu-latest, "Test Bash wrapper postflight and parity" (postflight-safe.mjs bash) took:
  - 44:48 (run 41830422144 at 060d7b8c, 12:39:47 to 13:24:35Z);
  - 44:52 (run 41823611051 at 2037e856);
  - 45:50 (run 41834653023 at 80078651, 13:29:43 to 14:15:33Z).
  That is 75-76% of the 60-min execFile cap (postflight-safe.mjs:51), and it grows with every wrapper row. CQ-M07r/s/t are adding postflight scenarios right now.
- The job has no timeout-minutes in ci.yml, so the cap at :51 is the only bound.
- The fix should leave real headroom on all three postflight steps, not just the two Windows ones. That could be a per-step budget, an env-overridable cap, or splitting the suite across steps/jobs.
- Get the runner timings with `gh.exe run view <id> --json jobs`.
